Ashen Swale retains control of el objetivo for 10 minutes. Este control ends immediately if el objetivo loses the unconscious condition or el objetivo is dealt an additional 50 daño since Ashen Swale took control (which destroys the body completely). After he has lost control of a target, that target is permanently immune to Corpse Puppet.

Ashen Swale can control up to two targets with Corpse Puppet at a time.

Jealous guardians of tombs, barrows, and sepulchers, cairn wights usually spawn from necromantic rituals. For those mortals who cannot abide the thought of separation from their earthly possessions, the undead existence offered by transformation into a cairn wight can be tempting. Perhaps as frequently, particularly avaricious and wealthy royalty or merchants seek out victims to transform into cairn wights to guard their precious wealth for all time.

Only in the rarest instances is the greed of a mortal strong enough to spontaneously transform them into a cairn wight without a dark ritual or the intercession of a powerful divine being. On those occasions, however, the resultant wight exhibits unmatched viciousness and likely owns rare treasure indeed.

As guardians of material possessions, cairn wights are supernaturally bound to the armaments they wore during the ritual used to create them. They can spread their necromantic powers into the armas they wield. A slash from a cairn wight's sword channels life from the victim into the wight.

Corrupted Elder Tree.name: Corrupted Elder Tree
Corrupted Elder Tree.publicNotes:
Arboreal regents-also called treants-are lumbering, solitary criaturas responsible for guarding an entire forest. They take an especially long view of affairs and never act brashly or without much deliberation. They occasionally come together in small groups called groves to share news and pass their wisdom down to the arboreal wardens that have sprouted under their watch. In times of grave danger, all the groves in a region may gather for a great months-long meeting to plan and, eventually, act upon a threat.

The typical arboreal regent is 30 pies tall, has a trunk 2 pies in diameter, and weighs 4,500 pounds.

Arboreals are guardians of the forest and representatives of the trees. As long-lived as the woods they watch over, arboreals consider themselves parents and shepherds of trees rather than their gardeners. Consequently, while arboreals tend to be slow and methodical, they are terrifyingly swift when forced to fight in defense of the woods. Though they rarely seek out the companionship of short-lived folk-even elves are fugacious in the eyes of arboreals-and have an inherent distrust of change, arboreals have been known to tolerate those who seek to learn from their long-winded, rambling monologues, especially if such pupils also express a desire to protect the timberlands. Against those who threaten their realm, such as loggers eager to harvest lumber or settlers aiming to establish croplands or a town, arboreals' wrath is unwavering and devastating. Perhaps ironically, arboreals are gifted at tearing down what others build-a rasgo that serves vengeful members of their kind well.

Arboreal wardens are the rangers of arboreal SOCIETY. Estos itinerant folk have an innate curiosity about the woodlands in which they dwell, and rarely stop to take root and rest in the same part of the forest twice. Este wanderlust makes wardens ideal forest patrollers and scouts. While they are robust combatants, they know better than to confront dangerous foes on their own. Instead, they report any dangers to arboreal regents. In rare cases, large groups of arboreal wardens congregate to form a copse. Copses travel beyond the boundaries of a forest to investigate the hinterlands and gather INTELLIGENCE on potential threats before returning to report their findings. Arboreal wardens do not pretend to understand to other criaturas' motives-like most forces of the natural world, they are ambivalent about mortal affairs that do not involve their forest.

Arboreals are guardians of the forest and representatives of the trees. As long-lived as the woods they watch over, arboreals consider themselves parents and shepherds of trees rather than their gardeners. Consequently, while arboreals tend to be slow and methodical, they are terrifyingly swift when forced to fight in defense of the woods. Though they rarely seek out the companionship of short-lived folk-even elves are fugacious in the eyes of arboreals-and have an inherent distrust of change, arboreals have been known to tolerate those who seek to learn from their long-winded, rambling monologues, especially if such pupils also express a desire to protect the timberlands. Against those who threaten their realm, such as loggers eager to harvest lumber or settlers aiming to establish croplands or a town, arboreals' wrath is unwavering and devastating. Perhaps ironically, arboreals are gifted at tearing down what others build-a rasgo that serves vengeful members of their kind well.

While most naiads lead solitary lives close to their chosen ward, sometimes these nymphs congregate in coven-like groups where river tributaries meet, performing great magic and blessing the waters of the land. Because naiads' bonds to their bodies of water permit more flexibility, they are the nymphs most likely to INTERACT with humanoids and even visit their settlements on occasion. Unlike other nymphs, naiads occasionally become adventurers, especially when dark forces seek to despoil NATURE or otherwise threaten the land, joining forces with others to prevent the corruption of NATURE.

Nymphs are a family of fey that take the form of beautiful humanoids with elven features and have a deep association with the natural world. The most common of their kind are the dryads, which are spirits that embody great trees, but many other kinds of nymphs exist, including naiads, who watch over bodies of water. All nymphs are guardians of some element of NATURE, typically a specific tree or pond, or even-in the case of nymph queens-whole forests or massive bodies of water.

Giant Tapir.name: giant Tapir
Giant Tapir.publicNotes:
With a blunt, prehensile trunk and a squat posture, giant tapirs resemble a cross between elephant and boar, though they're actually more closely related to horses and rhinoceroses. Tapirs live in loose herds that graze near rivers and lakes. They enjoy fresh water, not only for the lush plants that grow along the shores-which they eat in prodigious quantities- but also for the protection the water provides. When predators approach, tapirs retreat to the water to hide, keeping their snouts barely above the surface to breathe. Likewise, the breezes and scents that accompany creeks and rivers mask tapirs' musk as they travel along these waterways. Despite their ungainly movement, tapirs are remarkably sure-footed, easily traversing mud and similar terrain thanks to their broad toes.

Humanoids often hunt giant tapirs for their meat and durable hides. Such hunts are far from guaranteed, though; tapirs can run at least as fast as their hunters, and most will fight if cornered. The docile giants do what they can to avoid confrontation siempre que possible. If they sense danger approaching, giant tapirs make a loud whistling sound to warn other tapirs about predators. A community who befriends or domesticates a herd of tapirs can use this whistling habit as an alarm system against encroaching enemies.

giant tapirs are usually quite placid, but they can be fearsome when roused. Their tusk-like front teeth are suitable for gouging attackers, and a tapir that manages to get a mouthful of an enemigo's arm or leg can use its blunt molars to grind the flesh to paste. Tapirs have good hearing and an excellent sense of smell, but like many prey animals, they have poor vision. In the chaos of combat against multiple enemies, giant tapirs can become overwhelmed and confused, lashing out at allies as well as foes or fleeing the scene entirely.

Glyptodon.name: Glyptodon
Glyptodon.publicNotes:
Glyptodons are enormous, armadillo-like megafauna that roam sandy riverbanks and ancient forests in search of their favorite foods, namely riparian grass and tender saplings. Surly and suspicious, glyptodons avoid predators not out of a defensive instinct-their armored hides protect them from most well-equipped carnivores-but rather because they simply prefer to be left alone to their placid foraging. Despite their great size, glyptodons can survive on surprisingly little food, and they'll eat just about anything. As a result, they're more likely to be encountered roaming across vast tundra or desert regions than other large herbivores, appearing as a single, lumbering hump against an otherwise-flat horizon.

A glyptodon's scutes-the thick, bony plates of its carapace-grow in distinctive patterns and scar readily, making it easy for non-glyptodons to identify individual animals. Glyptodons have notoriously bad eyesight, even for prey animals, and rely on their sense of smell to get around and identify threats and each other. In combat, they primarily rely on their thick carapaces to protect them from attackers.

Although southern merchants have occasionally attempted to create a glyptodon-mounted trading network, riding these giants is an exercise in frustration, as their rounded hides provide little purchase for humanoid riders' pies or saddles. However, some webbed-toed people of the plains, including bands of lizardfolk, have managed to maintain glyptodon mounts thanks to their strong, flexible, clawed pies. Other ancestries primarily view glyptodons as a source of meat and tough hides, the latter of which make for excellent impromptu shelters and river boats.

When cornered, a glyptodon uses its powerful digging claws to scrape or scare away attackers. Glyptodons can use their tails to ward off smaller predators, but generally do so only as a last resort.

Groplit.name: Groplit
Groplit.publicNotes:
The groplit is a squat little animal shaped like a water droplet, with a bulbous rear end and an eel-like face that juts from a narrow skull. Its rear legs are more muscular than those in front, which it primarily uses for balance, giving it the gait and appearance of a toad. Groplits are best known for their greasy skin and queasy hygienic habits: they spend most of each day using their two long tongues to slurp up their own oily excretions or similarly viscous discharge originating from plants or other animals. Although they prefer to dwell in northern wetlands, fens, and moist caves, groplits can thrive in all but the most barren environments. They'll eat just about anything, though they tend to prefer small, crunchy animals like bugs and birds.

Groplits are famously loyal and highly sociable companions, and they make for dedicated, if somewhat odd-looking, pets. They can be taught simple commands and appear to take great pride in obeying them, performing stunts even in the face of obvious danger. An unscrupulous maestro might train a groplit with the intent to sacrifice it in an emergency, a fate to which the groplit is happily resigned. Este single-minded obedience and their slow reproductive rate make groplits fairly rare in the wild.

As a result of the way their bones are structured, groplits exhibit an imperturbable smile, of sorts-a physical feature which some find as creepy (or enraging) as others find it endearing. Its apparently ceaseless jubilation has given this criatura the nickname "the grinning toad" in some parts of the world.

Because they love to lap up oily matter of all kinds, groplits are naturally drawn to greasy animals like @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.tashopA1s2fAbSXA]{Slurks}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-bestiary-2.Actor.g1htYgARxNKxc7MV]{giant Slugs}, and lagofirs. For the most part, such animals rarely mind the company of an amiable groplit, though there's no such thing as a free meal; groplits who drop their guard amid their found family often end up on the wrong side of their companions' intestinal tracts.

Lagofir.name: Lagofir
Lagofir.publicNotes:
Lagofirs are semiaquatic omnivores that resemble a rabbit the size of a large dog. They're social criaturas, playful but territorial and protective of their kin. Lagofirs live in family units and gather in larger groups as often as their environment allows. They're commonly found in northern Avistan, congregating along rivers, lakes, and coasts, where they subsist on fish, crustaceans, marine plants, and small mammals.

Lagofirs have a stout body, rounded back, large hind legs, long ears, and a short, fluffy tail. Their powerful incisors are capable of cracking through clam shells, chitin, and bone. Both their front and back paws are webbed, and their front paws are highly dexterous, enabling them to grasp objects and perform simple manual tasks.

Lagofirs secrete a thick, sweet-smelling, flammable oil that coats their fur. Warm to the touch, this oil keeps them insulated and comfortable in frigid water and cold climates. Lagofirs mark their territory by brushing against solid surfaces, coating them in oil that, to other lagofirs, identifies an individual. Este makes their lairs, known as burrows or forms, incredibly hazardous. A single spark in a lagofir form can cause an explosion.

action->Consuming Fumes.description: 15 pies. The lagofir is surrounded by fumes from the flammable oil it exudes. After exploding, the fire source is extinguished.

action->Deep Breath.name: Contener La Respiración

action->Flammable.description: Lagofirs excrete a warm, flammable oil. Any criatura that Grapples a lagofir or is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} by a lagofir becomes coated in lagofir oil for 10 minutes or until the oil is washed off, which takes 1 minute of vigorous scrubbing. action->Nimble Rush.description: The lagofir attacks while darting around its foes. The lagofir Strides twice and Golpes at any point during its movement. It can substitute a Swim action in place of any Zancada.

Loblobi.name: Loblobi
Loblobi.publicNotes:
In the First World, rivers don't always flow as expected; sometimes they run backward, upward, or just disappear into mist and reappear somewhere else entirely. Fey native to such rivers are often just as capricious. Este quality is particularly true of loblobis, cunning carnivores who resemble small, chubby humans with the heads and wings of crested herons.

Estos malicious tricksters love playing any pranks that result in other criaturas being embarrassed, hurt, or even drowned. Their most common "antic" is to cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Seaah9amXg70RKw2]{Water Walk} on a hopeful river-crosser, only to dismiss the conjuro when their victim has traversed halfway across. Conversely, most loblobis are terrible sports when they're the butt of a joke. It's common wisdom that few criaturas can hold a grudge like a loblobi.

Exceptionally vain, loblobis flutter and dance constantly to show off their plumage. Failing to comment on a preening loblobi's appearance is a sure method to invite eternal enmity, but flattery might buy enough time to sneak away from the evil fey.

Long-horned Bison.name: Long-horned Bison
Long-horned Bison.publicNotes: Much like their smaller bison cousins, long-horned bison are bovines with short faces, two horns, a shaggy coat, and a noticeable hump on their back. Despite their relation to more placid bovines, however, long-horned bison are ill-tempered and territorial. Their tread shakes the ground, while the thunder of their stampedes can be mistaken for an earthquake. Long-horned bison weigh upwards of 4,500 pounds and measure up to 9 pies tall and 16 pies long. Their horns, measured tip to tip, can be almost as wide as the bison are tall.

action->Shadow Blend.name: Shadow Blend

Necrohusk.name: Necrohusk
Necrohusk.publicNotes:
Necrohusks are skittering, undead monstrosities, created when a humanoid is purposefully twisted into a new criatura through necromantic experimentation. Unlike fleshwarps and recipients of successful necrografts, prospective necrohusks never survive the procedure. After reanimation, they're cunning, animalistic criaturas that follow their creator's orders without question.

Creating a necrohusk is an incredibly difficult endeavor, fraught with error. Most attempts result in lumps of useless, rotten slurry or malformed undead no more cunning or dangerous than a mundane zombie. The costs in time, experimental subjects, and expensive conjuro components lead some would-be necromancers to conclude that the results aren't worth the risk. Occasionally, spellcasters can harness the power of the Void during the process, which lessens the monetary cost but vastly increases the danger, often producing a deadly backlash resulting in the creator's death and a masterless necrohusk.

Among the Sutaki, only Ashen Swale and his lieutenants, Turkek and Azi, have the skill and knowledge to create necrohusks with any regularity, although Turkek's interests often lead him away from such gruesome endeavors. Necrohusks are created from volunteers in Ashen Swale's cult or from traitorous Sutaki whom Ashen Swale wants to punish with a ghastly fate.

Rime Sludge.name: Rime Sludge
Rime Sludge.publicNotes:
Rot and decay play a natural role in swamps of all climates, and latent magical energies or other strange phenomena can transform decomposing matter into oozes and other monstrous criaturas made of living muck. Tundra wetlands are no exception to this trend. Worse, in such regions, a quick freeze can prevent noxious sludge from breaking down, and sequential years of short, seasonal thaws can compress rot upon rot until the pestilential mass animates as a rime sludge. Estos rare, noxious oozes hungrily search for and consume any organic matter they find in their northland habitats.

Like most oozes, rime sludges consist primarily of protoplasm, though theirs has a slushy consistency peppered with disgusting nuggets of indigestible matter, such as petrified wood, jagged arrowheads, and animal fossils. A rime sludge renews this protoplasm by consuming plants and animals and maintaining a careful balance of semifrozen decomposition in its mutable form.

Rime sludges are among the few oozes that thrive in cold climates, as too much heat accelerates their natural decay. Rime sludges can't survive temperatures too far above freezing for more than a few days. Rising temperatures force them to migrate toward cooler climates or cold underground areas.

Few intelligent criaturas inhabiting cold climates want anything to do with rime sludges. Estos oozes can't be entrenado, tend to wander off at random, and emit a noxious stink at the slightest hint of warmth. Some inventive criaturas try to trap rime sludges in pits to keep them contained and use them to dispose of prisoners or food scraps. Because of the oozes' overpowering stench, these pits tend to be quite deep.

action->Motion Sense 60 feet.name: Motion Sense 60 pies

action->Noxious Sublimation.name: Noxious Sublimation
action->Noxious Sublimation.description: The first time each round that the rime sludge takes daño de fuego, a cloud of sickening decay roils outward, dealing @Damage[2d6[poison]|options:area-damage] daño (@Check[fortitude|dc:17|basic|options:area-effect]) to all criaturas in a @Template[emanation|distance:10]. A criatura that fails its tirada de salvación is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 3} on a critical failure).

action->Slushy Undulation.name: Slushy Undulation
action->Slushy Undulation.description: A rime sludge ignores difficult terrain and greater difficult terrain from ice and snow and doesn't risk falling @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} when crossing ice.

Desencadenante A criatura holding the rope pulley pulls it

Roru.publicNotes: Rorus, sometimes called hunter demons, are brutal fiends that arise from the souls of mortals who mutilated animal corpses. action->Predatory Aura.name: Predatory Aura
action->Predatory Aura.description: 30 pies. An animal or beast entering or starting its turn in the emanation must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:25] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 1} (asustado 2 on a critical failure). Asustado animals within the emanation can't attack the roru. A criatura that succeeds at a tirada de salvación against predatory aura is immune for 24 hours.

action->Incite Ferocity.name: Incite Ferocity
action->Incite Ferocity.description: The roru focuses its corruption on an animal or beast it can see within 30 pies. The criatura must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:25] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for [[/r 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}. The confused criatura can't attack the roru. A criatura that succeeds at its tirada de salvación is temporarily immune to Incite Ferocity for 24 hours.

action->Wear Pelt.name: Wear Pelt
action->Wear Pelt.description: The roru dons the pelt of an adjacent dead animal, transforming into its lookalike. The roru becomes the same size and gains the same Velocidades as el objetivo animal. The roru loses its claw and jaws unarmed Golpes and gains the types of melee Golpes of the animal whose pelt it wears. The Golpe deals daño equal to the roru's jaws Golpe or, if the Golpe has the agile rasgo, the roru's claw Golpe. Either way, the tipo de daño changes to match the new ataque sin armas. While a roru wears a pelt, half of daño físico dealt to the roru is instead dealt to the pelt. A pelt has Hardness 5 and 25 HP. When a pelt reaches 0 HP, the roru is immediately expelled from the pelt and it is destroyed.

Shattering Rune.name: Shattering Rune
Shattering Rune.description: A magical rune is inscribed on the tarry earth at the entrance to the hut, buried beneath snow, with an @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.zJxUflt9np0q4yML]{Invisible} sensor that detects criaturas within a 10-pies-radius sphere.
Shattering Rune.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:30|name:Erase the Rune|traits:hazard] (maestro) to erase the rune without triggering the sensor or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (5th rank; counteract DC 28) to dispel the rune

action->Shattering Shockwave.name: Shattering Shockwave
action->Shattering Shockwave.description:
Desencadenante A Small or larger criatura comes within 10 pies of the rune

Efecto The rune unleashes a deafening peal of thunder that deals @Damage[10d8[sonic]] daño in a 20-pies burst (@Check[reflex|dc:30|basic]).

action->Rhinoceros Charge.name: Rhinoceros Charge
action->Rhinoceros Charge.description: The rhino Strides twice, then makes a horn Golpe. As long as the rhino moved at least 20 pies, the Golpe's daño increases to @Damage[(3d12+5)[piercing]]. A Medium or smaller criatura struck by this attack must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:22] save or be automatically Shoved back 5 pies and knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} by the force of the blow.

Spectral Archers.disable: @Check[intimidation|dc:31|traits:haunt,hazard] (experto) to cow the archers into fleeing or @Check[religion|dc:28|name:Banish the Spirits|traits:haunt,hazard] (experto) to temporarily banish the spirits
Spectral Archers.reset: The haunt vanishes permanently if the graveknights are destroyed. Otherwise, it returns after 1 hour.

action->Rain of Bolts.name: Lluvia de virotes
action->Rain of Bolts.description:
Desencadenante A criatura attacks the graveknights in area G1 or enters the castle

Efecto The haunt makes a spectral bolt Golpe against the triggering criatura, then rolls initiative.

action->Routine.name: Routine
action->Routine.description: (1 action) The hazard fires one bolt at every criatura in a 30-pies-by-30-pies area in front of the gate as 1 action. Because the spectral archers fire bolts continuously, the haunt can also use the Continuous Barrage free action (below) to fire bolts at each criatura during that criatura's turn.

action->Continuous Barrage.name: Continuous Barrage
action->Continuous Barrage.description:
Desencadenante A criatura in front of the gate finishes an action

Efecto The haunt makes a spectral bolt Golpe against the triggering criatura.

action->Solstice Dependent.name: Solstice Dependent
action->Solstice Dependent.description: An hora is mystically bonded to a natural location with a simple astronomical calendar that marks the summer and winter solstice. If they aren't at that location at dawn when the sunlight touches the calendar, they become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1}, increasing the value by 1 for each missed day and reducing by 1 only when they witness dawn's light touch the calendar. Even on a cloudy day, there's enough sunlight to satisfy the hora's need. An hora can perform a 24-hour ritual to bond to a new location.

action->Summer's Salvation.name: Summer's Salvation
action->Summer's Salvation.description:
Desencadenante The summer hora or an ally within 30 pies that the summer hora can see fails a Perception check or tirada de salvación

Efecto If it's the month of the summer solstice, the hora's or ally's check retroactively gains a +4 bonificador de estado, which can change the outcome from a critical failure to a failure or a failure to a success. If it's the month before or after the summer solstice, the check gains a retroactive +2 bonificador de estado instead. In the other months except during the three winter solstice months, the check gains a retroactive +1 bonificador de estado instead. During the winter solstice months, this ability has no effect. The summer hora can't use Summer's Fortune again for [[/gmr 1d4 #rounds]]{1d4 rounds}.

Hora queens rule over wide stretches of land, nourishing and protecting native animals and plants. Most hora queens watch over their regions in pairs: one summer and one winter, or one autumn and one spring.

action->Tied to the Land.name: Tied to the Land
action->Tied to the Land.description: A summer hora queen is intrinsically tied to a specific region, such as a forest or hilly plain. For 3 months around the summer solstice, the environment is supernaturally resilient, allowing the queen to automatically attempt to counteract conjuros and rituals that would harm the environment, such as @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.7yWXx3qC4eFNHhxD]{Blight}, with a +27 counteract modifier and a counteract rank of 7. For the 3 months around the winter solstice, however, her warded region becomes twisted or unhealthy unless a winter hora queen is present.

action->Focus Beauty.description: The hora queen focuses her beauty upon a target within her aura. The criatura must attempt a Will save. On a failure, it is affected as if by the hora queen's nymph's beauty aura; if it was already affected by the aura, it's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} until its sight is restored via restore senses or similar effect, or until the hora queen chooses to remove the effect using a single action, which has the concentrate rasgo. A hora queen can Focus Beauty on a given criatura only once per turn.

action->Inspiration.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.IFQd4GiHlV33p7oK]

A nymph queen can inspire a single intelligent criatura by giving that criatura a token of her favor, typically a lock of her hair. As long as the criatura carries her token and remains in good standing with the nymph queen, the criatura gains a +1 bonificador de estado to all CRAFTING checks, PERFORMANCE checks, and Will saves.

If a nymph queen grants her Inspiration to a bard and the nymph queen is that bard's muse, the bard gains an additional benefit depending on their muse theme: for LORE muse, the bard also gains a +1 bonificador de estado to all LORE checks; for maestro muse, the bonificador de estado to PERFORMANCE checks increases to +2 for the purpose of determining the effects of compositions; for polymath muse, the bard gains a +4 bonificador de estado to untrained pruebas de habilidad; and for all other muses, the Will save bonus increases to +2 against fey.

Syarstik can't leave Red Cat Cave, and he rarely ever leaves area E9

A typical ghost can stray only a short distance from where it was killed or the place it haunts. A typical limit is 120 pies. Some ghosts are instead bound to a room, building, item, or criatura that was special to it rather than a location.

action->Rejuvenation.name:

When Syarstik is destroyed, he re-forms after [[/br 2d4 #Syarstik Rejuvenation]]{2d4 days} within area E9, fully healed. Syarstik can be permanently destroyed only by a non-possessed wielder of the Primordial Flame.

action->Awaken Painting.name: Awaken Painting
action->Awaken Painting.description:
Syarstik animates a cave painting within 60 pies for 10 minutes. The painting's movement mimics Syarstik's, so the connection between the ghost and the awakened painting is obvious. Las criaturas other than Syarstik within 10 pies of the awakened painting are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Desprevenido} because of these eerie movements. Syarstik can make ghostly fangs Golpes at any criatura within 10 pies of a cave painting; el objetivo's cover or concealment from the cave painting, rather than from Syarstik, applies to this Golpe.

A criatura adjacent to an awakened painting can spend 2 actions to attempt a @Check[occultism|dc:18|name:Compel Awakend Painting|traits:concentrate|overrideTraits:true] or @Check[religion|dc:18|name:Compel Awakend Painting|traits:concentrate|overrideTraits:true] check (to compel the awakened painting to abate) or a @Check[crafting|dc:20|name:Smear the Cave Painting|traits:concentrate|overrideTraits:true] or @Check[thievery|dc:20|name:Smear the Cave Painting|traits:concentrate|overrideTraits:true] check (to thoroughly smear the cave painting). On a success, the painting is destroyed, and the animation ceases. Either way, this activity has the concentrate rasgo.

Destroying three awakened paintings quells Syarstik's anger, causing the great cat to cease his attacks.

action->Pounce.name: Pounce
action->Pounce.description: Syarstik Strides and makes a Golpe at the end of that movement. If he began this action @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Escondido}, he remains hidden until after this ability's Golpe.

action->Sneak Attack.description:

action->Motion Sense.name: Motion Sense
action->Motion Sense.description: A tar ooze can sense nearby motion through vibration and movement.

action->Sticky.name: Sticky
action->Sticky.description:
Desencadenante The tar ooze is hit by a melee attack

Efecto The ooze attempts to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.PMbdMWc2QroouFGD]{Grapple} the criatura that hit it. The ooze must still spend an action to extend the duration of the GRAB on subsequent rounds, as normal.

action->Viscous Sludge.name: Viscous Sludge
action->Viscous Sludge.description: The tar ooze can have up to eight criaturas grappled at the same time; doing so doesn't prevent it from making pseudopod Golpes. A tar ooze can CLIMB on ceilings and other inverted surfaces, though such surfaces are difficult terrain.

action->Zombification.name: Zombification
action->Zombification.description: A criatura slain while engulfed by a tar ooze undergoes a horrifying transformation and crawls from the ooze a week later as a tar zombie.

Tar Pit.name: Tar Pit
Tar Pit.description: A 15-pies-wide patch of tar covered with dirt and leaves attempts to capture criaturas that step onto it.

A criatura that was submerged up to its waist becomes submerged up to its neck, and a criatura that was submerged up to its neck is pulled under and must hold its breath to avoid suffocation. Other criaturas can Aid the criatura, typically by using a rope or similar aid or by attempting to pull the criatura out with their own @Check[athletics|dc:33] check, with the same results as if the criatura attempted the check. In addition to the usual results, a character adjacent to the tar pit who critically fails while Aiding moves into the tar pit. A criatura that Climbs out of the tar pit escapes the hazard and lands @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} in an adjacent space.

Throttled Blindheim.name: Throttled Blindheim
Throttled Blindheim.publicNotes:
Inhabitants of damp, subterranean caves, blindheims resemble stubby humanoids with oversized, frog-like heads and bulbous eyes. Their eyes emit a soft glow at all times, but a blindheim can draw back the heavy membrane that normally covers them to emit an intense light as bright as day. Estos simple criaturas use their lights to draw in or disorient prey, mostly small animals like lizards, rodents, or fish. However, they might go after larger prey if trying to feed their young. When they encounter criaturas their own size or larger they retreat, flashing their eyes to facilitate their escape if necessary. They often hunt in pairs or small packs. Using their lights to coordinate from a distance, they slowly close in on the criaturas they hunt. One common hunting pattern involves one blindheim diving deep and using its light to chase fish to the surface, while another up above snatches them up and tosses them onto the land to eat later.

Blindheims make their nests in damp caverns, especially grottoes next to underground lakes or bogs. An ideal nest rests in a cozy cavern with plenty of fungus to eat, a few fish swimming in a lake, and the comforting drip of water from the ceiling. Blindheims prefer to lead quiet and serene lives, and even when first born they emit only the meekest of vocalizations. A blindheim is born shining, and its parents cuddle over it to dim the light so as to avoid attracting predators.

It's not just animals that endanger blindheims. Underground peoples find the criaturas useful and attempt to capture them for specialized purposes. Duergars use them as "raid frogs," placing heavy hoods over blindheims' heads and revealing them suddenly during raids to blind their foes. They sometimes send the criaturas along with their slaves that lack darkvision into the mines as a source of light. Drow use them for some of these same purposes, and some nobles have been known to treat the criaturas as mere lanterns, having them hoisted to the ceilings of their halls. Neither duergars nor drow take good care of the captive criaturas, so blindheims rarely last long in captivity.
